name: Dredge Mining Collective ConduitStrike VX-2 Deep Aquifer Thermoelectric Tap
product_name: Dredge Mining Collective ConduitStrike VX-2 Deep Aquifer Thermoelectric Tap
description:
The ConduitStrike VX-2 is a deep-bore thermoelectric energy extraction system engineered specifically for Meridian 88's Great Lakes basin geology, exploiting the substantial thermal differential between deep confined aquifer water — maintained at a consistent 4–7°C year-round by bedrock insulation — and the urban heat island surface environment, which regularly exceeds 38°C in summer peak periods. Each VX-2 installation consists of a 180–240 meter drill casing fitted with bismuth telluride thermoelectric generator (TEG) modules arrayed along the casing exterior in thermally conductive contact with both the cold aquifer water column and a peripheral heat-exchange sleeve connected to surface thermal infrastructure. The temperature gradient drives Seebeck-effect current generation continuously, producing 12–30 kW per bore depending on depth, seasonal differential, and surface heat source intensity. Multiple bores are typically clustered in arrays of 4–8 units to supply a meaningful district-scale output.

The VX-2 improves on the Dredge Mining Collective's earlier VX-1 prototype primarily through its Articulated Casing Seal System (ACSS), which prevents aquifer contamination from surface thermal fluids — a regulatory failure that caused significant legal and environmental liability in the VX-1's limited field trials. The ACSS uses a multi-stage polymer gasket and pressure-equalization valve assembly that has passed Meridian 88 Environmental Compliance Authority certification, allowing VX-2 installations to operate in proximity to potable water infrastructure that would have been off-limits to the earlier design. Dredge Mining markets the VX-2 as a 'passive perpetual generation' asset — no fuel, no moving parts in the primary generation loop, and maintenance intervals of 18–24 months under standard operating conditions.

The primary clients are mid-scale commercial building operators, arcology sub-grid managers, and industrial facility owners seeking to reduce Ouroboros Energy grid dependency. The Dredge Mining Collective retains ownership of all installed VX-2 systems under a power-purchase agreement model, selling output back to clients at rates competitive with municipal grid pricing — a business structure that gives the Collective a growing footprint of distributed generation assets embedded beneath the city's commercial core.
enables: Reduced Ouroboros Energy billing leverage over commercial clients
social_impact: The ConduitStrike VX-2 has introduced a quiet but significant power struggle — both literal and political — between the Dredge Mining Collective and Ouroboros Energy. As more commercial clients sign VX-2 power-purchase agreements, Ouroboros loses billing leverage over exactly the high-consumption commercial accounts that subsidize grid maintenance in lower-tier residential zones. The practical consequence is that Tier 3 and 4 residential grid reliability has declined as commercial cross-subsidy revenue drops, while the Collective's sub-surface asset portfolio grows. Environmental advocates have also raised concerns about cumulative thermal extraction effects on the Great Lakes aquifer system — concerns the Collective's Environmental Compliance Authority certifications explicitly do not address at scale.
story_hooks: A Dredge Mining Collective survey crew drilling a VX-2 bore beneath a Garnet District commercial block breaks into a sealed pre-Meridian 88 tunnel system — and the equipment starts picking up heat signatures that shouldn't be there at that depth

Ouroboros Energy has begun quietly acquiring the buildings directly above clusters of VX-2 installations, raising questions about whether they intend to interfere with the bore casings or are simply trying to recapture the generation assets through real estate control

The ACSS seals on a cluster of VX-2 installations in the Ironworks District have been deliberately compromised — thermal fluid is slowly contaminating a confined aquifer that feeds three Tier 3 residential water reclamation systems, and the sabotage is being covered up

A Dredge Mining Collective engineer approaches a fixer with evidence that the VX-2 power-purchase agreements contain a hidden clause allowing the Collective to remotely throttle output to any client during 'grid stress events' — a killswitch over the buildings of anyone who signed
